en: The Eight Verses on Govinda
Truth, knowledge, infinite, eternal, formless yet the supreme space;
effortless yet the ultimate exertion, restless with the play of the courtyard and the quadrangle;
though fashioned into various forms by *māyā*, it is formless and yet the very form of the universe.
Bow down to Govinda, the supreme bliss, the lord of the earth who is himself without a lord. || 1 ||
[He is] the one who, as a child, experienced the terror of being struck by Yaśodā with a lump of clay;
he whose face, when opened, beheld the entire range of the fourteen worlds;
he who is the foundational pillar for the cities of the three worlds; and he who is the Lokāloka mountain, yet is beyond all worldly perception.
Bow down to Govinda, the Lord of the World, the Supreme Lord, the supreme bliss. || 2 ||
The destroyer of the enemies of the gods of the triple heaven, the remover of the earth's burden, the healer of the disease of worldly existence;
absolute liberation, whose food is butter yet who is without food, the sustainer of the world;
the unmanifest radiance of the specific transformations of the mind when it is clarified and free from impurity.
Bow down to Govinda, the Śaiva, who is exclusively peaceful and supreme bliss.
The cowherd, the cowherd who is the embodiment of the Lord’s divine play, the protector of the lineage;
the cowherd cherished by the pastimes of sporting with the gopīs and by the act of lifting Govardhana Hill; he whose many names, such as Govinda, are clearly proclaimed by the cows.
Bow down to Govinda, the supreme bliss, who wanders upon the paths frequented by the cowherd girls.
It is the breaker of the circle of cowherd girls' assemblies, appearing as non-dual even while existing in a state of duality;
its auspicious beauty is ever greyed by the dust kicked up by the hooves of cattle;
it is inconceivable bliss grasped through faith and devotion, whose true nature is contemplated.
Bow down to Govinda, the supreme bliss, whose greatness is like that of the wish-fulfilling gem.
As the two of them were preoccupied with bathing, he took their garment and ascended the mountain.
Then, as they— clad only in the directions as their clothing— desired to give it back and drew near to seize it,
he [the Buddha], who had shaken off the delusion of the two-fold sorrow and dwelt within the reach of awakening, [remained there].
Bow down to Govinda, whose body is pure existence and who is supreme bliss.
I bow to the Beloved, the cause of all causes, the beginningless beginning, Time itself, who is without form;
who dances repeatedly upon the head of the serpent Kāliya in the Yamunā;
who is Time yet transcends the divisions of time, who has encompassed everything and destroys the evils of the Kali age.
Bow down to Govinda, the supreme bliss, who is the cause for the realization of the three periods of time.
In the land of Vṛndāvana, I worship Him who is worshipped by the hosts of the most exalted gods,
whose nectar-like bliss is a gentle smile as pure as jasmine, who delights His friends,
and whose pair of feet are the object of veneration for the minds of all venerable great sages.
Bow down to Govinda, the ocean of all virtues worthy of veneration, the supreme bliss.
He who studies this *Goviṃdāṣṭaka* with his mind dedicated to Govinda—
[calling out] "Govinda, Acyuta, Mādhava, Viṣṇu, O Leader of Gokula, Kṛṣṇa!"—
has all his sins washed away by the nectar-water of meditation upon Govinda’s lotus feet.
He approaches that Govinda, who abides within as the nectar of supreme bliss.
Thus ends the Śrīgovindāṣṭaka composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
